extracted_by: hand, T-0335 — the Democrat read, August 1835
note: Vol. II No. 16, the first Democrat after the scene month. THE ISSUE'S TOWN MATTER IS THE ADVERTISING, and this is the printing of the month where the standing advertising block is read whole: the attorneys' cards, the two forwarding houses, the boot stores, the auction house and the paper's own imprint are claimed HERE and, where they stand unchanged in the three later issues, are not re-claimed from them (the same discipline T-0293 used for November 1834). Later issues carry the matter that is new. THE POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST stands across page 3 columns 2 and 3 over J. S. C. Hogan's signature, and its HEADING ALONE is claimed here (c027). This setting reads the date as 'ys list uay of Duby 1a', which a hurried reading takes for the first day of July; the 26 August printing sets the same heading legibly as the THIRTY-FIRST day of July 1835, and all four August printings carry that one standing list, identical name for name and in the same order. Its roughly six hundred names are NOT minted here or from any other printing in this ticket — T-0299 measured that minting a standing list once per printing turned 298 names into 638 persons in the 1834 read — and T-0336 owns the name-level extraction from ONE named printing. The page 3 prices current is set in this issue without its Building Materials block and is too broken to read at figure level, so the month's prices are claimed from the 12, 19 and 26 August printings instead. NOT CLAIMED: the page 1 and page 2 miscellany, which is reprinted eastern matter, and the presidential land-sale proclamations on page 4 column 6, which concern townships outside Cook County.

claims.notes: TWO NOTICES ON ONE FRAGMENT, AND THEY ARE CLAIMED TOGETHER BECAUSE THE SEGMENTER RAN THEM TOGETHER: the fire-insurance agency's body follows its heading across a line break and the hardware notice begins on the same line. THE HARDWARE FIRM IS NEW — 'have formed a connection in the mercantile business, under the firm of Jones, King & Co' — and its stock arrives by the Brig Illinois, so the goods on its shelves in August 1835 came off a lake vessel this season. Three partners are named where the imprint on page 4 of this issue calls the firm 'Jones & King'. No address is given in the notice itself; the paper's own imprint places the firm's hardware store on South Water Street (claim c020). AND THE AGENCY ON THIS FRAGMENT IS NOT THIS FIRM'S (T-0410). Until that ticket the fire-insurance card's own sentence — 'having been appointed Agent for the Howard Fire Insurance Company' — stood here as this claim's `announces_opening`, and so the register read Jones, King & Co. as having been appointed the Howard's agent over a dateline of 1 July 1835. The fragment says otherwise: the card is signed '[E]. K. [H]UBBARD.' and the hardware notice below it is signed WILLIAM JONES, BYRAM KING, W. B. CLARKE, and this claim's own entity list already reads 'UCBRARB,' as 'Hubbard, E. K.' with the role 'insurance agent'. The appointment was the agency's and it now lives in identity.json's `agencies` as the fifth printing of E. K. Hubbard's holding, with Jones, King & Co. recorded there as a refused holding. The firm's own opening is announced by its formation notice at 1835-07-08 c009 and 1835-07-22 c009, which this change does not touch. Nothing of the quote, the normalized reading or the entities moves — only the sentence that was read onto the wrong one of the two notices.

placement.note: The fire-insurance card and the hardware notice beside it print no address. The business-level `street` is not read back into the placement (T-0859).

claims.notes: THE PAPER PLACES ITSELF, AND IT IS THE ONLY IMPRINT IN THE MONTH THAT DOES. The Democrat's office stands on South Water Street over Jones & King's hardware store — the firm that announced itself as Jones, King & Co. on page 3 of this same issue (claim c008), and the same frontage J. Curtiss's law office is entered from (claim c017). So one South Water Street building carries a hardware store on the ground floor and at least two upstairs tenants, one of them a printing office with a press in it. The words supplied — 'street, over' and 'store' — are the two the column cut, and 'over' rather than 'opposite' is read from the preposition's length and from Curtiss's '(up stairs)' on the same frontage; it is bracketed and it is the least certain word in the claim.

claims.notes: THE FIRST OF FOUR PRINTINGS OF ONE STANDING LIST, and the heading is claimed rather than the six hundred names beneath it. This column sets the date as 'ys list uay of Duby 1a', which a hurried reading takes for the FIRST day of July; the 26 August printing sets the same heading legibly as the THIRTY-FIRST day of July 1835 (chicago_democrat_1835_08_26.json c008), and the name lists of all four printings are identical name for name and in the same order. So the four August Democrats carry one list, the postmaster's return for the end of July, standing in the forme for a month. The names are NOT minted from this printing or from any other in this ticket: T-0299 measured that minting a standing list once per printing turned 298 names into 638 persons in the 1834 read, because the identity policy correctly keys on the whole normalized name and the segmenter cuts each printing differently. T-0336 owns the name-level extraction and will make it from ONE printing. J. S. C. Hogan's signature closes the list in the next column.
